mainEntity.name: Who is affected by the January 1, 2027 Florida Citizens flood insurance requirement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Effective January 1, 2027, under Florida Statutes § 627.351(6), all remaining Citizens Property Insurance personal residential policyholders with wind coverage must carry separate flood insurance, regardless of FEMA flood zone (including Zone X) or Coverage A dwelling value.

mainEntity.name: Are Florida condominium unit owners exempt from the Citizens 2027 flood mandate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Personal HO-6 condominium unit-owner policies, HO-4 tenant contents policies, and policies excluding windstorm coverage are exempt from the personal Citizens flood mandate, though condo associations remain subject to master insurance and lender warrantability standards.

mainEntity.name: How much did Citizens HO-3 insurance rates drop in South Florida in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under Florida OIR-approved 2026 filings effective on renewals on or after July 1, 2026, Citizens HO-3 average renewal rates declined roughly 13.0% in Miami-Dade, 12.6% in Broward, and 11.7% in Palm Beach, though individual premiums vary by roof age, wind mitigation, and territory.

mainEntity.name: How does the 20% Citizens takeout rule affect South Florida home sellers and buyers?

acceptedAnswer.text: If an approved private insurer offers comparable coverage within 20% of the Citizens premium, the homeowner or buyer is generally ineligible for Citizens. Because private carriers do not require flood insurance in low-risk Zone X, a private policy with strong wind-mitigation credits can sometimes lower a buyer's total monthly escrow.

@graph.description: FHFA raises 2027 Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach conforming loan limits to $855,400. Compare purchase-price ceilings, jumbo rules, and seller strategy.

@graph.name: Carlos Uzcategui - United Realty Group

Miami-Dade Broward and Palm Beach Real Estate

mainEntity.name: What is the 2027 conforming loan limit in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach?

acceptedAnswer.text: On November 24, 2026, FHFA set the 2027 baseline conforming loan limit for Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties at $855,400 for 1-unit properties, $1,095,250 for 2-unit duplexes, $1,323,900 for 3-unit triplexes, and $1,645,350 for 4-unit fourplexes, effective January 1, 2027.

mainEntity.name: How expensive a home can you buy in South Florida before needing a jumbo loan in 2027?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the $855,400 limit applies to the loan balance rather than the sale price, a 1-unit buyer can purchase up to $900,421 with 5% down, $950,444 with 10% down, $1,006,353 with 15% down, $1,069,250 with 20% down, or $1,140,533 with 25% down before crossing into jumbo territory.

mainEntity.name: Do South Florida condominiums qualify for the $855,400 2027 conforming loan limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, eligible warrantable condominiums and townhomes share the $855,400 1-unit limit, provided the association clears Fannie Mae Full Review or Freddie Mac project standards covering insurance, reserves, and Florida Milestone Inspection and SIRS compliance. Non-warrantable buildings still require cash or portfolio loans.

mainEntity.name: How should South Florida sellers priced between $900,000 and $1,140,000 use the 2027 loan limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sellers in Weston, Doral, Fort Lauderdale, Miami, Plantation, and Boca Raton can align asking prices or targeted closing-cost credits so 10% to 20% down buyers keep their loan at or below $855,400, avoiding jumbo reserve requirements and expanding qualified financed demand.

@graph.headline: South Florida New Construction vs. Resale: Rate Buydowns and Seller Concessions (2026)
@graph.description: Compare South Florida builder 2-1 rate buydowns vs. resale seller concessions at 7.28% rates under Fannie Mae B3-4.1-02 and FHA 6% limits.

@graph.name: Carlos Uzcategui - United Realty Group
knowsAbout: Miami-Dade Broward and Palm Beach Real Estate

mainEntity.name: Is a seller-funded 2-1 mortgage rate buydown more effective than a price cut in South Florida?

acceptedAnswer.text: On an illustrative $700,000 home with 20% down ($560,000 loan at 7.28%), a $20,000 asking price cut lowers monthly principal and interest by $109. A seller-funded 2-1 buydown costing roughly $13,218 (1.89%) lowers Year 1 payments by $729 per month and Year 2 by $373 per month while costing the seller $6,782 less and preserving comparable sales.

mainEntity.name: How much can a Florida home seller contribute toward a rate buydown under Fannie Mae and FHA rules?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-4.1-02 for primary residences and second homes, seller concessions (including temporary buydowns) are capped at 3% above 90% LTV, 6% from 75.01% to 90% LTV, and 9% at 75% LTV or less, with a 2% cap on investment properties. FHA loans allow a flat 6% seller or builder concession cap. Concessions cannot fund down payments.

mainEntity.name: What should South Florida buyers verify before accepting a builder rate buydown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buyers should compare the builder's captive-lender Loan Estimate against an independent lender quote to check origination fees and base pricing, confirm ongoing CDD and HOA fees, budget for full improved-value property tax reassessment, and verify whether closing occurs before December 31, 2026 for Florida Amendment 3 homestead residency timing.

mainEntity.name: Do buyers still need to qualify at the full mortgage note rate on a 2-1 buydown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Conventional and FHA underwriting requires borrowers to qualify at the full permanent note rate rather than the reduced Year 1 promotional payment. Consult a licensed mortgage loan officer to verify exact program eligibility and payment schedules.

@graph.description: Navigate Fannie Mae Full Review, 0.9% FHA condo eligibility, and Florida's Dec 31, 2026 SIRS cutoff across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach.

@graph.name: Carlos Uzcategui - United Realty Group
knowsAbout: Miami-Dade Broward and Palm Beach Condominiums

mainEntity.name: Why do so few South Florida condos qualify for FHA or conventional loans in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: According to MIAMI REALTORS® and HUD data, only 21 of 2,397 condo buildings (0.9%) across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach hold active FHA approval. For conventional loans, Fannie Mae retired Limited Review on most projects over 10 units, requiring a Full Review of reserves, master insurance, HOA delinquencies, litigation, and critical repairs.

mainEntity.name: What is the December 31, 2026 Florida condo SIRS deadline under HB 913?

acceptedAnswer.text: Associations with three or more habitable stories that coordinate their Structural Integrity Reserve Study (SIRS) with a required Milestone Inspection must complete the SIRS no later than December 31, 2026. HB 913 raised the structural reserve-item cost threshold to $25,000 and allows a temporary reserve-contribution pause of up to two consecutive annual budgets by majority owner vote following a milestone inspection to prioritize urgent repairs.

mainEntity.name: How can a condo seller close cleanly if a building is non-warrantable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sellers in non-warrantable buildings should disclose Milestone Inspection, SIRS, and assessment status upfront, price accurately against competing cash-closing inventory, and leverage global MLS syndication to reach all-cash domestic and international buyers—who already account for nearly half of Miami-Dade condo closings and 82% at $1 million and above.

mainEntity.name: What documents should a South Florida condo buyer review before waiving contingencies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buyers should obtain the completed Phase 1 and Phase 2 Milestone Inspection reports, the current SIRS study, adopted annual budget, reserve balances, master insurance declaration page, recent board meeting minutes, and a pre-offer lender check against Fannie Mae Form 1076 requirements. Legal review of association documents belongs with a Florida real estate attorney.

mainEntity.name: Should a South Florida homeowner sell in late 2026 or wait until spring 2027?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your property is single-family or a reserve-compliant condo, listing during the late-2026 winter arrival window captures cash and relocation buyers before spring inventory rises further and while 7.28% mortgage rates sideline competing leveraged listings.

mainEntity.name: Why are condo prices softening while single-family medians hold firm?

acceptedAnswer.text: Miami-Dade condo supply sits at 12.7 months versus 5.4 months for single-family homes, driven by stricter agency lending reviews and December 31, 2026 SIRS reserve deadlines that shift leverage toward cash buyers.

mainEntity.name: Do lower Citizens insurance rates help home sellers right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Approved 2026 Citizens rate reductions (-8.7% HO-3 and -10.4% HO-6) alongside private-market depopulation reduce buyer carrying-cost friction when paired with current wind-mitigation documentation.

mainEntity.name: Does a 7.18% national mortgage average determine my home’s value?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A national mortgage average is financing context. Property-specific pricing requires current competing listings, recent comparable sales, condition and transaction terms.

mainEntity.name: Does Miami’s historical price growth show that mortgage rates do not matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A long-run house-price index does not measure current rate sensitivity or establish the value of a particular property.
